entries.claim: Hypothesis A (motivated, untested): the previous z-mediated generator predicts all 63 future latents in one pass from (s_0, G, tau); the candidate instead initialises a latent state z_hat_0 = I(s_0, G) and advances it with a learned residual transition z_hat_t+1 = z_hat_t + F(z_hat_t, G, tau_t..tau_t+4), trained and run as a free 63-step rollout on its own predicted latents with no teacher forcing.

caveats: Untested: no run of the experiment has finished; the hypothesis must be presented as a motivated current hypothesis, never as a result.

The transition is not a function of z_t alone: it also reads G and a 5-frame window of the given object trajectory (frames t..t+4, i.e. a 4-frame look-ahead of tau). s_0 enters the stateful path only through z_hat_0.
The stateful model observes nothing during the rollout; it feeds back its own predicted latent. It is not closed-loop on observations and not teacher-forced.

z_hat_0 comes from a separately trained module with the Stage-1 encoder's architecture, not from the Stage-1 encoder (the predecessor report had proposed allowing z_0 = E_z(s_0) at inference; the running study does not do that).

The transition is a residual MLP, not a transformer or recurrent network; chosen before training for rollout time and memory (the measurement is recorded only as a sentence in the code). Look-ahead k = 4 is not swept.
The stateful models are smaller than the whole-sequence models (design bound in the code: within 15 % of the parameter count).

The predecessor report cautions: "The diagnostic did not show that an iterative model would beat Stage 2" and "A rollout feeds its own errors back" (z_joint_decoder_followup/report.md, Section 19, lines 743-744, 754).

entries.claim: Hypothesis B (motivated, untested): the previous decoder rebuilds every contact map from z_t and the geometry alone, C_t = D_abs(z_t, G_t), without access to the given s_0; the candidate keeps the known initial map and decodes only its change, C_t = s_0 + D_delta(s_0, z_hat_t, G_t), with s_0 added as a per-point input and a zero-initialised output so that the model starts as contact persistence.

entries.metric: Design facts only. What the hypothesis predicts, per the template: M01 better than M00 and M11 better than M10 on dense error E_C (lower is better), most of all in the first frames (frames 1-16 bin in the code's rule).

TACO and ARCTIC | Hypothesis B as writte.value: "Hypothesis B: decoding throws away s_0. The absolute decoder has to rebuild the initial dense realisation from a 64-D latent that does not keep every detail, although s_0 is given. Decoding only the change from s_0 keeps that detail. It predicts that M01 beats M00 and M11 beats M10, most of all in the first frames."

TACO and ARCTIC | Absolute decoder (M00,.value: B0 absolute decoding C_t = D_abs(z_t, G_t): per-frame point-token transformer over 512 points (tokens = geometry of frame t), FiLM on [G | z_hat_t]; the Stage-1 D_z blocks (loaded) + 2 identity-initialised blocks, width 256

TACO and ARCTIC | s_0-preserving decoder.value: "residual (B1) tokens = geometry of frame t | s_0 at that point -> Delta_C_t ; C_t = s_0 + Delta_C_t. The s_0 channel is a new input column (zero-initialised) and the output layer is zero-initialised, so the model starts as contact persistence C_t = s_0."

TACO and ARCTIC | Predecessor limitation.value: "The path was fixed. The decoder sees ẑ, G and the geometry tokens of the object, not s_0. A decoder that also sees s_0, or a temporal network that starts from the encoded s_0, was not tested. The first-frame deficit is therefore part of every result here."

TACO and ARCTIC | Objective of M01.value: L_C + lambda_z L_z; L_C = MSE in the residual units rho = (C - s_0) / sigma_r on 4 random future frames per sequence per step (all 63 at validation)

caveats: Untested: no run of the experiment has finished; present as a motivated current hypothesis.

"Discards s_0" is true of the decoding step only: in the previous model the temporal backbone is conditioned on s_0 (and the stateful path derives z_hat_0 from s_0); what the absolute decoder lacks is direct access to the dense s_0.
G_t in the formulas is the frame's per-point geometry tokens (512 x 10 channels) together with the static vector G; it is not the same object as G alone.
The two decoders are the same family and size (6 blocks, width 256); the s_0-preserving one differs by one input column.

The predecessor report notes a limit of any z-mediated model: "with ideal predictors, decoding alone cannot do better than direct prediction in dense error. The realistic target is the TACO pattern: equal dense error with better structure, without the early-frame loss" (z_joint_decoder_followup/report.md, Section 19, lines 755-757).

entries.claim: The two hypotheses are motivated by earlier finished studies, read per dataset. After the decoder was adapted, the z-mediated model was similar to the direct model in dense error on TACO (E_C 1.698 vs 1.700, verdict similar, with better structure / wrench) and worse on ARCTIC (2.158 vs 1.890, 14.2 % worse). On both datasets its latent error is small on training sequences and large on test sequences (z RMSE 0.088 vs 0.702 on TACO, 0.064 vs 0.717 on ARCTIC), and it is worse than the direct model in frames 1-8 (dense-error gap 0.294 on TACO, 0.481 on ARCTIC). Given the true current z, a learned predictor improves on persistence on TACO at 4 and 8 frames ahead (11.3 % [10.0, 12.5] and 17.8 % [16.5, 19.1] lower RMSE); on ARCTIC the gain is not distinguishable from zero at 4 frames (0.2 % [-4.0, 4.0]) and small at 8 frames (6.9 % [1.6, 12.2]). These are window-averaged direct predictions from the true latent, not rollouts; the predecessor report states that the diagnostic 'did not show that an iterative model would beat Stage 2' and rates the stateful test 'a reasonable next test on TACO and a weak one on ARCTIC'.

entries.claim: The experiment's code contains a decision rule written down in advance. A paired difference on identical test sequences counts as better or worse only if it is at least 2 % and its 95 % take-cluster bootstrap interval excludes zero; this threshold is the rule of the previous studies and the template describes it as fixed before any result was read. From these verdicts the code assigns each dataset an outcome: A (stateful is the main fix), B (s_0 preservation is the main fix), C (both help: M11 better than M00, M01 and M10), E (nothing beats M00 or D0), or 'mixed' when none applies; D (stateful helps on TACO only) is a separate statement about the two datasets together. The timing cannot be checked independently: the code directory is not under version control and was still being edited while the runs were in progress.

entries.claim: Apart from the two factors, the four z models share the earlier setting: the same data, split, 64-frame sequences, Stage-1 teacher latents, decoder family and size, optimiser, 100 000-step budget with no stop before 25 000 steps, selection on validation L_C, seed and evaluation code, and z only (no r, no diffusion, no new latent). Each factor is a bundle rather than a single change. The stateful level replaces the transformer backbone by an initial-state module plus a residual-MLP transition, adds the loss term L_z0, has fewer parameters (stated design bound: within 15 %), and sees a local window of the object trajectory instead of the whole trajectory. The s_0-preserving level both feeds s_0 to the decoder and decodes a change from s_0. The reused direct reference D0 was trained under the older 80 000-step budget.

dataset_differences: The experiment covers TACO and ARCTIC only (DATASETS = ("taco", "arctic")); OakInk2 is not part of it.

The plan asks for the two datasets to be read separately: "The two datasets entered this experiment with different prior evidence, and the plan asks for them to be read separately" (narrative_templates/04_taco_arctic_prior.md line 1).

Prior evidence for Hypothesis A differs by dataset: probe gain over persistence from the true z_t at 4 / 8 frames is 0.1128 / 0.1782 on TACO and 0.0019 / 0.0694 on ARCTIC (z_temporal_diagnostic). Template: TACO "has state-dependent latent dynamics that a local predictor can learn. The stateful hypothesis has its best chance here"; ARCTIC "is locally close to persistence. There the plan expects the s_0-preserving decoder to matter more than the stateful change, and allows for the direct model to stay ahead."

Starting point differs: the reused z model M00 is similar to the direct model D0 in dense error on TACO (E_C 1.6978 vs 1.7004, verdict similar) with better structure / wrench (decision answer "yes"), and worse on ARCTIC (E_C 2.1584 vs 1.8901, relative -0.1419, verdict worse; structure "worse") (z_joint_decoder_followup).
Early-frame gap of M00 against D0 in the first eight frames: 0.2940 on TACO, 0.4813 on ARCTIC (z_joint_decoder_followup/report_values.json).
ARCTIC only: 21 of the 44 test takes come from a subject absent from training; TACO has none (z_temporal_diagnostic/report.md line 525; template 04 line 9).
Split sizes differ: TACO 1312 train / 141 val / 364 test sequences (186 test takes); ARCTIC 1005 / 106 / 186 (44 test takes).
One outcome label, Case D ("stateful helps TACO only"), is by design a statement about the two datasets together; it compares the per-dataset answers and does not pool numbers.

The reused direct reference D0 was trained to 80000 steps on TACO and stopped by patience at 48000 on ARCTIC; on ARCTIC the predecessor report says the reused D0 "may understate the direct model there", which is why the partial retrained row D0r exists as a sensitivity check.
Status differs: both stateful runs are running on TACO, both are still pending on ARCTIC (queue order puts TACO first); M01 is running on both datasets.
Model sizes differ slightly by dataset (input dimensions): M01 75967553 (TACO) vs 75877697 (ARCTIC); M10 69829249 (TACO) vs 69230209 (ARCTIC, from a discarded attempt's header).
The predecessor report rates the stateful test "a reasonable next test on TACO and a weak one on ARCTIC" (z_joint_decoder_followup/report.md lines 736-737).
do_not_claim: Any result, direction or size of effect of the 2 x 2 experiment (e.g. 'stateful z improves ...', 's_0-preserving decoding fixes early frames', 'M11 is best'): 0 of 6 runs have finished and no test metric of this study exists.

Any preliminary value: validation readings in the training logs or W&B, pilot RMSEs / ratios in init_aug_decision.json, the dry-run metric files in a scratch directory outside the result tree, or numbers from the discarded attempts.
That M00 is a new or retrained run: it is the reused M2 of the z joint-decoder follow-up; only M01, M10 and M11 are trained here. D0 is also reused.
That the previous model 'discards s_0' or 'does not use s_0': only its decoder lacks s_0; the whole-sequence temporal backbone is conditioned on s_0.

That the stateful model is 'closed-loop', 'feedback-controlled', 'teacher-forced' or 'conditioned on observed contact during the rollout': it is a free rollout that feeds back its own predicted latent and depends on (s_0, G, tau) only.

That the stateful model starts from the Stage-1 encoder (z_0 = E_z(s_0)): z_hat_0 comes from a separately trained module with the same architecture; the Stage-1 encoder is not part of the model or of inference.

That the transition is a transformer or a recurrent network with a hidden state, or that z_t+1 depends on z_t alone: it is a residual MLP on the 64-D latent state that also reads G and a 5-frame object-trajectory window (4-frame look-ahead).

That the hypotheses are established causes of the earlier shortfall ('the problem is open-loop prediction', 'the cause is the loss of s_0'): the templates call them remaining, untested architectural assumptions; one planned outcome is 'neither'.

That the experiment is expected to make z-mediated generation beat the direct model: the predecessor report says the diagnostic 'did not show that an iterative model would beat Stage 2' and names as the realistic target 'equal dense error with better structure, without the early-frame loss' (the TACO pattern), and calls the test weak on ARCTIC.

That the decision rule is formally pre-registered or externally time-stamped: it is a dict in a code file that was untracked when this was checked; supported wording is 'fixed in code before any result was read' (the template's claim, not independently verifiable).

'No test quantity was computed before training ended' as a factual statement about the project: a pipeline dry run produced test-part metric files from early snapshots in a scratch directory (selection is nevertheless on validation L_C only).
Pooled or averaged TACO + ARCTIC statements; Case D compares per-dataset answers and is not a pooled number.
That OakInk2 is part of this experiment.
That r, diffusion, new latents or extra losses are involved: the study uses z only, with L_C + L_z (+ L_z0).
That results are multi-seed or cross-validated: one training seed on one fixed split; a second seed is conditional on the ambiguity rule.
That 'z_1:T' frames are predicted with T the window length: 63 future frames (1..63) of a 64-frame window are generated; frame 0 is the given s_0.
That the stateful and whole-sequence models have identical capacity: the stateful models are smaller (design bound in the code: within 15 %).
That the absolute and s_0-preserving decoders differ in size or family: same 6-block width-256 decoder, one extra input column.

That the stateful runs have been running since the first launch: all stateful runs were discarded and restarted from step 1 at 15:44-15:47 on 2026-10-04 after an initialisation defect was found; the discarded runs are used nowhere.
Describing the s_0-preserving change as r, 'noise removal' or a 'null-space' residual: Delta_C_t is the decoded change of the contact map from s_0, nothing more.
Calling z 'disentangled' or 'independent' when describing why it is kept: the sources use a 64-D structure latent from Stage 1; stay with 'structure-oriented'.

attached_by_the_verifier: The stateful factor is not a single change (design facts from the code, to attach wherever the 2 x 2 is described): besides carrying a state it (a) replaces the transformer backbone with an initial-state module I plus a residual-MLP transition F, (b) adds the loss term L_z0, (c) has fewer parameters (TACO total 69 829 249 vs 75 967 297 for M00; design bound 'within 15 %'), and (d) changes how much of the object trajectory is visible: the whole-sequence backbone uses unmasked self-attention over all 63 frame tokens (cf_models.py lines 26-60, s2_models.py lines 50-56), while the transition at step t reads tau_t..tau_t+4, i.e. object motion from t-8 to t+12 (narrative_templates/06_architecture.md lines 10-12). A difference between M10 and M00 could therefore not be attributed to statefulness alone.

The decoder factor is two changes made together: s_0 as a per-point decoder input and the output re-defined as a change from s_0 (06_architecture.md lines 23-25, 'The same decoder with two changes'). The experiment does not separate them.

The direct reference D0 already decodes a change from s_0: 'C_hat_t = s_0 + sigma_r rho_hat_t', with a zero-initialised head so that it 'starts as the persistence predictor C_t = s_0' (s2_models.py lines 9-10; zj_common.py line 49). Template 02 lines 15-16 says the direct model 'starts from s_0'. Hypothesis B gives the z path something the direct model already has; worth one sentence in the motivation.

The extractor's caveat on the transition input ('5-frame window of the object trajectory, frames t..t+4, a 4-frame look-ahead') is incomplete. Each tau feature is itself a summary of object states from 8 frames before to 8 frames after its frame, so the template (edited at 16:06, after the extraction) now states that the transition at step t 'sees object motion from t-8 to t+12 and nothing about hands or contact'.

Intervals for the ARCTIC motivation numbers were not delivered: probe gain over persistence at 4 frames 0.0019 with 95 % interval [-0.0400, 0.0396] (includes zero), at 8 frames 0.0694 [0.0161, 0.1217] (z_temporal_diagnostic/persistence_comparison.csv). Also not delivered: the diagnostic's own qualification that the TACO label is 'Case A (borderline)' and that the gains are window averages (z_temporal_diagnostic/report.md line 26).

'Pre-registered' has no independent evidence. There is no dated plan document in the repository (the templates refer to 'the plan', which is not a file there), git tracked no file of scripts/research/z_stateful_s0_factorial/, when this was checked (first committed on 2026-10-04) zf_common.py (the DECISION dict) was last modified at 15:31 and zf_aggregate.py (which turns verdicts into cases) at 16:06 on 2026-10-04, and a decision_summary.csv dated 16:07 exists in the dry-run scratch directory. Supported page wording: 'a decision rule written into the experiment's code in advance'; avoid 'pre-registered'.

The case logic in code is more specific than the one-line labels: a dataset's answer is the '+'-join of the cases that apply or 'mixed' when none does; A requires both stateful comparisons better, the decoder effect not 'yes' and M11 not better than all three others; B is the mirror; E requires that no trained model is better than M00 and the best z model (chosen on validation E_C) is not better than D0; D is a separate yes / no row over the two datasets (zf_aggregate.py lines 161-173, 298-301). The two-pair reading can also return 'mixed', which the DECISION strings fold into 'else no' (zf_aggregate.py lines 120-126).

The early-frame reading of this experiment uses frames 1-16 (zf_common.py lines 39, 86), while the predecessor's 'first eight frames' gap used frames 1-8. Do not present the 0.294 / 0.481 gap as the quantity this experiment's rule will test.

Terminology: the code calls the whole-sequence model '(open-loop)' (zf_common.py line 4), but the stateful rollout also receives no observation during generation, and the predecessor diagnostic calls this kind of rollout 'closed-loop' (z_temporal_diagnostic/report.md line 523). If the page uses 'open-loop', it should say what it means (all 63 latents predicted in one pass, no latent state carried forward) and should not call the stateful model closed-loop or feedback-controlled.

Page notation to fix: z_1:63 of a 64-frame window (not z_1:T); C_t = D_abs(z_t, G_t), where G_t is the frame's per-point geometry tokens together with the static vector G; 'z_t -> z_t+1' needs the note that the transition also reads G and the local object trajectory and that z_hat_0 comes from a separately trained module, not from the Stage-1 encoder.
